svg.title: Palestinian Armed Struggle (1968–72): Karameh, Dawson's Field, Black September & Relocation to Lebanon
svg.desc: Edexcel GCSE History Option P5 cartographic map showing the Battle of Karameh in the Jordan Valley (21 March 1968), the PFLP triple airliner hijacking at Dawson's Field near Zarqa (6–12 September 1970), Black September urban fighting in Amman (September 1970), the Syrian armoured incursion near Irbid and Ramtha repelled by Jordanian forces, and the expulsion and relocation of the PLO to Southern Lebanon ("Fatahland") and Beirut (1970–71).

g.text: Driven from Jordan by mid-1971, PLO moves HQ
to Beirut & raids Israel from Southern Lebanon;
IDF raids Fatah camp across River Jordan;
Fatah & Jordanian guns kill 28 IDF troops →
famed moral triumph; Arafat leads PLO (Feb 1969).
King Hussein orders Bedouin army & tanks to shell
EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • OPTION P5: PALESTINIAN ARMED STRUGGLE (1968–72)
Karameh, Dawson's Field, Black September & Relocation to Lebanon
Strategic Shift: Expulsion from Jordan (1970–71) shifted PLO guerrilla bases to Southern Lebanon ("Fatahland") and spawned the covert Munich 1972 attack.
